name: Required partner presence and coexpression
description: Evidence that partners required by plausible functional systems are present in the relevant genome and expressed in matched conditions.
investigation_instructions:
Determine which functional systems are supported for the supplied gene or protein by investigating the presence and coexpression of partners those systems require. Start from the supplied sequence, selected file record or region, or snippets. No candidate annotation or searchable public name is required; plausible systems and their requirements can emerge from the investigation. Preserve the supplied material’s boundaries and establish its organism or sample context where available.

For each relevant system, identify the actual required partners from functional evidence, distinguishing indispensable components from optional or alternative ones. Do not declare a partner required merely because it is nearby, co-purifies or is often present. Keep the evidence defining the requirement separate from the evidence that the partner occurs in the target system.

Examine partner identities in the relevant genome using the actual loci, detected sequences or profiles and the scope of the search. Retain native match scores, E-values, coverage, matched regions and method limits where available. An incomplete assembly, unexamined region or missing annotation leaves presence unresolved; it does not demonstrate absence. Partner counts, when informative, must refer to the same explicitly defined required set and examined genome.

Examine whether the target and required partners are expressed together in the relevant matched samples and conditions. Retain measured expression, association statistics, units, normalization, sampling and replicate structure, and reported uncertainty or significance-test meaning. Unmatched samples, genomic adjacency and artificial coexpression during rescue do not establish native coexpression. Correlation does not demonstrate physical assembly or binding.

Use observed missing partners, condition-specific expression and alternative component systems to refine the possible role. Preserve when a required relationship is known only in a homologous system and explain the correspondence supporting its use for the target. Keep required-partner presence, expression together, physical interaction and demonstrated function distinct; missing expression data remain unknown rather than negative evidence.

evidence.limit: Full Results on nutritional dependence, pathway controls and FtsZ assays inspected. | Group source-use limits: Cellular perturbations and purified FtsZ assays are connected study outputs, not independent proofs of every causal link. Native sensing remains bounded.

evidence.observation: dinR loss induces the neighboring yneA-yneB-ynzC operon. Deleting that operon suppresses filamentation; inducible YneA alone reinduces elongation, whereas YneB or YnzC do not. Operon deletion reduces mitomycin-C-induced elongation.
evidence.limit: Primary publisher full Results inspected, including whole-operon deletion, separate gene re-expression and negative YneB/YnzC controls. The newer 2026 FtsW mechanism paper remains an abstract-only unexamined follow-up; do not treat the 2003 FtsZ inference as current direct mechanism. | Group source-use limits: Connected 2003 controls do not establish direct FtsZ binding. The 2026 FtsW follow-up remains abstract-only and unexamined; it is not upgraded by the older primary-results coverage.

evidence.observation: BtsT transported radiolabeled pyruvate specifically; purified proteoliposomes demonstrated proton-coupled uptake. CstA-related mutant selection and extracellular depletion established an additional route. Cold-starved cells accumulated BtsT and rapidly imported pyruvate; sensing-network mutants failed resuscitation under tested conditions.

Grouped as one investigation, not three cases. | Group source-use limits: Three papers form one connected investigation. No new transport fitting occurred; YhjX specificity remains unresolved.
